clue.text: Raised time to stroll briefly round, in European city

indicators.note: round says the shortened walk goes around the other pieces
briefly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to stroll is to walk
raised means upper, higher up

explanation.surface: A tourist strolls round a European city on a brief walk at some elevated hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' looks like it describes the time, but it supplies the word for higher; 'briefly' docks the last letter of the walk word, and 'round' makes it the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Wuppertal is an industrial city in western Germany, famous for its suspended railway.

clue.text: Yorkshire river stopped short of English moor

indicators.note: stopped short of says the river's name halts before reaching its final letter

parts.note: the Wharfe is a river in Yorkshire, northern England, flowing through Wharfedale

explanation.surface: A river in Yorkshire seems to stop just before reaching the English moors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moor' looks like a noun of the Yorkshire landscape, but it is the verb: to tie up a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to tie up a vessel at a landing place; a wharf is a quay, used as a verb for berthing.

clue.text: Get fit and grope around for one who would 17

indicators.note: around says the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone told to get fit and fumble about is the sort who quibbles over details.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the anagram signal for the seven letters plus the five beside them. The 17 refers to entry 17, which is the pedantic quibbling verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A pettifogger is a petty quibbler who argues over trivial points, just what a nitpicker does.

clue.text: Horse one's beginning to back in way-out display

indicators.note: in says the three small pieces are placed inside the way out

parts.note: a way out is an exit
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: beginning to means take just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A horse backs out through an exit at a show, one of its first moves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts H, I and B (the start of 'back') inside EXIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhibit is something put on display, and to exhibit is to display it.

clue.text: Hold it to cut out drawing

definitions.text: Hold it to cut out drawing

parts.words: Hold it to cut out drawing
parts.note: a drawn match is held to a deciding passage of play that eliminates the draw, as in tennis when the games are level

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep still so a drawing can be cut out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' suggests art, but here it means finishing level; the extra game decides a level set.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis the extra deciding game at six-all ends the possibility of a level outcome.

clue.text: Prime piece of pork in grease served up — I would like fat

indicators.note: in says the first letter of pork goes inside the turned grease
in a down clue served up means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: grease is oil

indicators.note: prime piece of means the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: I would contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: Pork served up in grease is just the thing for someone who wants fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' is a down-clue reversal; 'in' places the first letter of 'pork' within it, and 'I would' contracts as it would in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipoid is an adjective for substances resembling fat; chemists use it of fatty compounds.

clue.text: Deck hands trapped in cage with no opening

indicators.note: trapped in says the hands are held inside the cage
with no opening means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a coop is a cage for poultry
the right and left hands give R and L

explanation.surface: Sailors on deck are caught in a cage that has no way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no opening' cuts COOP to OOP, and 'trapped in' puts R and L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing ship, below the waterline.

clue.text: Image of a man crushed by a beast, one up amongst the best?

parts.note: an ox is a beast of burden
a man crushed by a beast has the beast on him, so on
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: A picture shows a man flattened under a beast, one of the elite at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the beast is written above the man, so the picture is of him lying beneath it. 'up' is the university sense: in residence at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford student is said to be up at university, and Oxford counts itself among the best.

clue.text: Get one over one's adversary in court

definitions.text: Get one over one's adversary in court

parts.words: Get one over one's adversary in court
parts.note: in tennis, to send the ball high over the head of the opponent at the net; surface reading is outwitting a legal opponent

explanation.surface: A lawyer outsmarts the other side in a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests a law court, but it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis player hits a high looping shot over an opponent standing at the net.

clue.text: Left in gunge, friends regularly get peas soaked?

clue.text: The most common element of Ho Chi Minh's character

definitions.text: The most common element of Ho Chi Minh's character

parts.words: The most common element of Ho Chi Minh's character
parts.note: of the letters in the name Ho Chi Minh, one appears three times, more than any other; that letter's spelt-out name is wanted

explanation.surface: A biographer asks what trait dominated the Vietnamese leader's personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like personality but means a letter; H appears three times in HO CHI MINH.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter H is written out in words as the name of that letter.

clue.text: Fear of Brussels closing region's chief plant

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union, EU

indicators.note: closing says the fear wraps round the next letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a phobia is a fear

indicators.note: chief means the leading letter of the word

explanation.surface: A dread of Brussels takes hold of the region's leading figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brussels' stands for the European Union, a common crossword convention; 'closing' means the fear word encloses the region's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphorbia is a large genus of plants, the spurges, including poinsettia.

clue.text: Gossip — one telling tales about criminal's last appeal, rejected before gallows

indicators.note: about says the liar goes round the following letter

parts.note: a fibber is someone who tells tales, or lies

indicators.note: last means the final letter of the word
rejected means the word is sent back, read backwards

parts.note: it is slang for sex appeal
a gibbet is a gallows

explanation.surface: A gossip whose tales led a criminal to a final appeal, refused before the hanging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes the liar enclose the final letter of 'criminal's'; 'rejected' turns the appeal word round, appeal being slang for sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A flibbertigibbet is a flighty, chattering person, an idle gossip.

clue.text: A result of early closure of corporation check to

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'A result of early closure of corporation check to (5-6)': it ends mid-phrase on 'check to' and the scan is blank, so the clue cannot be read in full

clue.text: Figurehead made of lead by loony? Not half

parts.note: to front something is to lead it

indicators.note: not half means half of the word is dropped, leaving its first three letters

parts.note: a loony is a maniac

explanation.surface: A ship's figurehead made of lead by a lunatic, only half finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' cuts MANIAC to MAN; 'made of' is a link, and 'lead' is the verb, not the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontman is a nominal leader who represents an organisation while others hold the power.

clue.text: One penalised in court for overstepping the mark

definitions.text: One penalised in court for overstepping the mark

parts.words: One penalised in court for overstepping the mark
parts.note: in tennis a server who steps on or over the baseline while serving is called for an infringement

explanation.surface: A defendant punished at trial for going too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests a law court; it is a tennis court, and the mark is the baseline.
explanation.definitionFit: This tennis infringement is the server's foot crossing the baseline, a penalty called by the line judge.

clue.text: Manipulator drops wife who looks for compliments

indicators.note: drops says a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a wangler is one who manipulates things to get his way

explanation.surface: A schemer leaves his wife for someone who craves flattery.
explanation.walkthrough: One fishes for compliments, so someone who fishes fits the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who fishes is said, idiomatically, to fish for compliments, so the fisherman is the seeker.

clue.text: Hardy's fine without audition?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
audition here is the sense of hearing, so without it is lacking ears

explanation.surface: A question whether Thomas Hardy's novel is fine without being tried out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' looks like the novelist, but it is the adjective bold; 'audition' means hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy can mean bold or daring, and someone without fear is bold.

clue.text: Vital force given up? Not at first

indicators.note: not at first means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: forgone means given up, gone without

explanation.surface: Life force abandoned, though not at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Orgone is Wilhelm Reich's term for a supposed universal life energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychoanalyst Wilhelm Reich claimed this was a cosmic energy permeating all living things.

clue.text: Can rising elite become pedantic?

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a can is a tin
the elite are the pick of the bunch

explanation.surface: A question whether an upwardly mobile elite will turn fussy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns TIN into NIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To nitpick is to be fussily pedantic over trivial details.

clue.text: Gave away painting — it's returned to you while asleep?

indicators.note: while asleep suggests being in bed, so the other letters go inside it

parts.note: one is asleep in bed

indicators.note: it's returned says the painting word comes back, read backwards

parts.note: painting is art
ye is an old word for you

explanation.surface: Someone sold off a picture which came back to them while they slept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'while asleep' works as the bed that holds the rest; 'it's returned' sends the painting word backwards, and 'you' is the archaic form.
explanation.definitionFit: To betray a secret is to give it away, reveal it.

clue.text: Metal layer, one with unusual casing

indicators.note: casing says the word for unusual wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: rum is old slang for odd or unusual
a hen is a layer of eggs
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A layer of metal has an unusual casing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' looks like a stratum of metal; it is a hen that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhenium is a rare, dense metallic element, named after the Rhine.

clue.text: Whines unpredictably, having not long been born

indicators.note: unpredictably says the letters fall into a random new order

explanation.surface: A newborn baby cries in fits and starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unpredictably' rearranges WHINES.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fairly new has been in existence only a short time.

clue.text: BA perhaps poet fails to finish: that may make his face red

definitions.text: that may make his face red

parts.note: a BA is an example of a first, undergraduate degree

indicators.note: fails to finish says the poet's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Robert Burns was a Scottish poet

explanation.surface: A poet who leaves his arts degree unfinished is left red-faced with embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red face' looks like embarrassment, but it is a mild scald or sunburn.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild burn affecting only the outer skin leaves it red and sore.

clue.text: Obscene name written with a pen

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: A rude name scrawled with a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like a writing tool, but it is an enclosure for pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty can mean offensive or obscene, as in nasty language.

clue.text: Eternal put-down of the Dutch in London

definitions.text: Eternal put-down of the Dutch in London

parts.words: Eternal put-down of the Dutch in London
parts.note: a permanent putting down is killing; in London's Cockney speech 'my old Dutch' is one's wife

explanation.surface: A Londoner forever disparaging the people of the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' looks like the people of Holland, but in Cockney slang (from 'duchess') it means a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin-derived word means the killing of one's own wife by her husband.

clue.text: Leaders of international boxing organisation held up belt

indicators.note: in a down clue held up means the letters read upwards, so backwards
leaders of means the first letter of each of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Bosses of a world boxing body have kept back a championship belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders of' gives IBO, which 'held up' turns into OBI.
explanation.definitionFit: An obi is a broad sash worn round the waist with a kimono in Japan.

clue.text: Stress being cut out, is getting around

indicators.note: getting around says the two letters of the small word wrap round the others
out signals that the letters of the word cut are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone stressed at being dropped goes out and about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles the three letters of 'cut', and 'getting around' makes the two-letter word wrap them; 'being' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ictus is the rhythmical stress on a syllable in verse.

clue.text: With tongue swollen, reportedly ill, having such a head?

indicators.note: said by someone whose tongue is swollen, the word comes out lisped, with an s heard as th

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: Someone with a swollen tongue, said to be ill, wonders whether this is a hangover.
explanation.walkthrough: A lisp turns S into TH. A thick head is the dull, aching head of a hangover or illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A muzzy, heavy head after drink or illness is called a thick head.

clue.text: Ready to keep mum

parts.note: ready is slang for cash, and cash given to keep someone silent is a bribe

explanation.surface: Someone willing to stay quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' looks like the adjective willing, but it is slang for cash (the readies).
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid to keep someone silent about something discreditable.
